title: About Austin Wade Smith
paragraphs: Austin Wade Smith is an engineer and writer building new alliances between people, ecology, and intelligent machines for a more interdependent and resilient planet. They are the author of Ecological Institutions, which traces how historic and emerging institutions shape the distribution of agency, value, and responsibility across human societies and the more-than-human world.

For five years, they served as Executive Director of Regen Foundation, leading systemic investment across an international network of grassroots DAOs. They are now the founder of River Computer, which builds tools so that bioregions, co-ops, and neighborhoods can hold their own data, make their own decisions, and direct their own money.

At River Computer, Austin is the primary architect of Waka, a system that links self-governed records and witness to programmable pools of capital. When agreed conditions are met, Waka can automatically release payments or issue certificates and credits. This work reflects a broader focus on epistemic and economic infrastructure for pluralism. Austin is interested in how intelligence, capital, and authority can remain grounded in many contexts rather than consolidated in a single center.

Austin has developed and advised on institutional, technical, and policy frameworks across Ecuador, Kenya, Uganda, Aotearoa New Zealand, and the United States. They have worked with Indigenous communities, technologists, NGOs, and public institutions on climate risk, habitat regeneration, and the agency of ecosystem stewards.
